+Plan §6.2 + head decisions. Registry mechanics here (vocabulary from Extras): merge with precedence (builtins reserved; provider < user < project), collision logging, near-miss matching, commandUpdates re-publication. Builtins bind to session surface: /compact → session.compact(), /context → usage/fill, /status → id/cwd/model/transcript path, /config (see below), /help. Dotfolder commands/*.md load via stack + untrusted Stencil as .prompt-only (data never becomes .action). Dispatch in this package's prompt() and exposed for frontend composers: leading /name routes through the registry BEFORE anything reaches the model — unknown /name errors with near-matches, never a model turn; /compact typed in an editor must never become a prompt.
+
+## Added 2026-07-28: `/config` and `/config export`
+
+Defaults now live in code with no shipped `config.yaml` (plan §4), so the agent must be able to write one on request — a default you cannot see is a default you cannot change. New builtin `.action`:
+
+- **`/config`** — print the effective merged configuration as commented YAML to the session. Read-only, no file written. This is the default with no arguments.
+- **`/config export home`** → `~/.config/<name>/config.yaml`
+- **`/config export project`** → `<session cwd>/.<name>/config.yaml`
+
+The emitter itself belongs to `AgentConfiguration` (task esq54zr); this task owns the command, its argument parsing, and its safety.
+
+**Writing a file is a side effect, and this is the one builtin that has one.** Rules:
+
+- If the target exists, **refuse and say so**; overwrite only on an explicit `--force`. A hand-edited config silently replaced by a machine-generated one is exactly the failure that makes people stop trusting a tool.
+- Create the containing directory when absent — that is not destructive.
+- Report the absolute path written, so the user knows which layer they just pinned.
+- An invalid or missing destination argument errors with the two valid values; never guess a location.
+
+`argumentHint` maps to ACP's `AvailableCommandInput` `{type: "text", hint: …}` (the `type` discriminator is required in v2). Consider a symmetric `/instructions export home|project` for the compiled-in system prompt (§6.0) — same problem, same shape.
+
+Tests:
+
+- [ ] `/config` prints without writing anything.
+- [ ] `/config export home` writes to the user layer; `project` writes to the project layer under the session's cwd, not the process cwd.
+- [ ] An existing target is refused; `--force` overwrites.
+- [ ] The written file decodes back to the same effective config (round-trip through the real command).
+- [ ] A bad destination argument errors and names the valid values.
+- [ ] No model turn and no transcript entries beyond what the action records.
\ No newline at end of file

@@ -1,4 +1,33 @@
 ---
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01kymg57zs9y1zb64cqxm2d29p
+  text: |-
+    **2026-07-28 — `commands/*.md` is DELETED as a source. Skills replaces it.**
+
+    Source 3 in this task's body ("Dotfolder templates … `commands/*.md`") is gone. The data lane is now **`FoundationModelsSkills`**: `~/.config/<name>/skills/<id>/SKILL.md` and `<project>/.<name>/skills/<id>/SKILL.md`, discovered over the same `DotfolderStack`, surfaced via `SlashCommandProviding`. One skill = one `/id` command. Skills is a strict superset of what the template lane offered (frontmatter validation, a real parameter model, `_partials/`, preload, bundled resources/scripts) over the same two directories with the same trust rules — two overlapping ways to define a prompt command was one too many.
+
+    **The trust boundary is unchanged**: skill markdown is data and can only ever produce a prompt, never `.action`.
+
+    ## Blocking gap found while reviewing this — Extras `c2pad49`
+
+    `SlashCommand.Body` has exactly two cases and **a skills provider fits neither**:
+
+    - Not `.prompt(template: String)` — the dispatcher would render it with Extras' Stencil engine, but Skills renders with its own pipeline and substitution model (`$0`/`$1`/`$ARGUMENTS[N]`/`$name`, `_partials/`, shell injection). Passing the raw `SKILL.md` body as a "template" produces **silently wrong prompt text**, not an error.
+    - Not `.action(...)` — documented as "runs code, streams text output, **never touches the model**," whereas a skill command's entire point is that the rendered body *becomes* the turn's input.
+
+    Needed: a third case, roughly `.rendered(@Sendable (Invocation) async throws -> String)` — the provider renders, the dispatcher feeds the result to the model as a normal turn. Filed on Extras as **`c2pad49`**. The trust tiers survive: a closure can only be constructed by linked Swift, so data keeps its single `.prompt` lane; the new case merely lets linked code produce model input instead of streamed output.
+
+    **This blocks skill-backed commands**, not the registry itself — builtins, merge/precedence, near-miss matching, and dispatch can all be built and tested against `.prompt` and `.action` first.
+
+    ## ACP argument fidelity — decided
+
+    Skills carries `SkillParameter { name, position, required, variadic, placeholder }` plus `acceptsTrailingArguments`. ACP v2's `AvailableCommandInput` is a single `{type: "text", hint: String}`, so a multi-parameter skill collapses to one hint. That is ACP's limit. **Decision: pass Skills' own `argument-hint:` string through verbatim** — it is already in the display syntax an editor wants (`<env> [region] [flags...]`), so the lossy step loses nothing a human reader needs. Structured prompting would be an `_meta` extension.
+
+    ## Precedence
+
+    The three-source order still holds (builtins reserved > linked providers > data), with Skills now occupying the data slot as a *linked provider that reads data* — its commands still cannot become `.action`. MCP prompts (`prompts/list` + `listChanged`) remain the reserved further source.
+  timestamp: 2026-07-28T13:55:49.369458+00:00

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01kyn02y8wxvda6njg5hfxgrj2
+  text: |-
+    **Spec audit — §10 Slash Commands (2026-07-28). One confirmation, one gap this task must close.**
+
+    **Confirmation — dispatch at the prompt owner is the only option the protocol allows.** "Users include commands as text messages in prompt requests using the slash prefix format (e.g. `/web agent client protocol`). **The agent recognizes and processes the command prefix accordingly.**" There is no invoke method; a command arrives as ordinary prompt text. So this task's core decision is not merely convenient — it is forced by the protocol, which is a stronger justification than the one currently written down.
+
+    Also: advertising is a **MAY**, not a MUST. `available_commands_update` is optional and "the Agent can update the list of available commands at any time during a session" — which is exactly what `commandUpdates` re-publication feeds.
+
+    **Gap — a command can arrive with other content attached.** "Commands can be accompanied by other message content types simultaneously." So a prompt may be `[text("/deploy prod"), resource_link(...), image(...)]`. This task says "a leading `/name` routes through the registry" and stops, leaving the remaining blocks undefined. They behave differently by body kind:
+
+    - **`.prompt` / skill commands expand into a model turn** → the extra blocks ride along into that turn after expansion. Dropping them discards the file the user deliberately attached to the command they ran.
+    - **`.action` commands take no model turn** → attached content has nowhere to go. **Do not silently discard.** Either refuse the invocation with a message saying this command takes no attachments, or hand the blocks to the action and let it decide. Refusing is the safer default; silence is the only option that is definitely wrong.
+
+    Add to acceptance criteria and tests:
+    - [ ] `/name` plus additional content blocks → for a `.prompt`/skill command, the extra blocks appear in the expanded turn.
+    - [ ] `/name` plus additional content blocks → for an `.action` command, the invocation is refused with a clear reason (or handled explicitly), never silently dropped.
+
+    Field shapes confirmed: `AvailableCommand` requires `name` + `description` (`input` optional); `AvailableCommandInput`'s text variant requires `hint`, which is where Skills' `argument-hint:` lands verbatim; custom input types must begin with `_`, and clients unable to render an input spec should preserve the metadata.
+  timestamp: 2026-07-28T18:34:11.100471+00:00
